title: Homeostasis: Keeping the Body in Balance Assessment Exam
description: Checkpoint assessment for Homeostasis: Keeping the Body in Balance.

questions.question: A student says, 'My temperature rose during exercise, so homeostasis failed.' What is the best correction?
options: A temporary rise can trigger responses that return temperature toward the healthy range.
Any change means the body has no regulation.
Homeostasis only controls blood sugar, not temperature.
Exercise stops all body systems from working.
questions.explanation: Homeostasis includes temporary change and response.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents a homeostatic response?
options: change detected -> signal sent -> response occurs -> condition moves toward range
response occurs -> no signal -> condition ignored -> system stops
trait inherited -> species changes -> fossil forms -> population grows
food eaten -> no digestion -> no absorption -> no energy
questions.explanation: Regulation requires detection, communication, response, and adjustment.

questions.question: The hormone that helps lower blood glucose after a meal is ________.
questions.explanation: Insulin helps cells take in glucose from the blood.

questions.question: Water balance can be part of homeostasis.
questions.explanation: Water balance is an internal condition that must be regulated.

questions.question: A person becomes dehydrated after heavy sweating. Explain one homeostatic response that could help.
questions.correctAnswer: The person may feel thirst and the kidneys may conserve water by producing less urine, helping restore water balance.
questions.explanation: The response should address water balance.

questions.question: Which organ pair is most directly involved in controlling breathing rate in response to carbon dioxide?
options: brain and lungs
bones and hair
teeth and skin
stomach and nails
questions.explanation: The brain detects changes and the lungs adjust gas exchange.

questions.question: Which is the best evidence that a body response is regulatory?
options: The response reduces or corrects the original disturbance.
The response is random and unrelated.
The response always makes the disturbance larger.
The response happens only once in life.
questions.explanation: Regulation moves a condition toward a workable range.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a homeostasis indicator and a homeostasis response.
questions.correctAnswer: An indicator is a measurable condition such as temperature; a response is an action such as sweating that helps adjust the condition.
questions.explanation: The answer should separate measurement from action.

questions.question: Which condition would most directly threaten cell function if not regulated?
options: blood pH moving too far from its safe range
the color of a shirt
the day of the week
the brand of a notebook
questions.explanation: Cell chemistry depends on safe pH ranges.

questions.question: The nervous and endocrine systems can both contribute to homeostasis.
questions.explanation: The nervous system sends rapid signals; the endocrine system sends hormonal signals.

questions.question: Homeostasis keeps conditions within a healthy ________, not at one exact value forever.
Use cause and effect to explain how the body responds to a hot environment.
questions.correctAnswer: Heat raises body temperature, sensors detect the change, and responses such as sweating and widened skin blood vessels release heat so temperature moves back toward the healthy range.
questions.explanation: A strong answer includes change, detection, response, and result.
